long_biography.plain_text:
Nasser Al-Rashid studied civil engineering at the University of Texas at Austin before joining King Fahd University of Petroleum and Minerals. He combined teaching with responsibility for campus construction and later became a dean. In Riyadh, his consultancy built its reputation by delivering complex public projects to demanding royal timetables.

His philanthropy grew from personal experience. After losing sight in one eye, he supported ophthalmic care and orbital-vision research, alongside liver research, hospitals and university engineering programmes. At flynas's 2025 flotation, he remained a substantial direct shareholder, extending his business interests beyond the engineering practice that created his wealth.
long_biography.html:
Nasser Al-Rashid studied civil engineering at the University of Texas at Austin before joining King Fahd University of Petroleum and Minerals. He combined teaching with responsibility for campus construction and later became a dean. In Riyadh, his consultancy built its reputation by delivering complex public projects to demanding royal timetables.

His philanthropy grew from personal experience. After losing sight in one eye, he supported ophthalmic care and orbital-vision research, alongside liver research, hospitals and university engineering programmes. At flynas's 2025 flotation, he remained a substantial direct shareholder, extending his business interests beyond the engineering practice that created his wealth.

uncertainties: No dedicated Forbes person profile was found. Forbes supplied a strong identity bridge through Lady Moura and Rashid Engineering, but its article does not establish a verified personal fortune and no net-worth estimate is used.

Public reference sources disagree on whether Al-Rashid was born in 1937 or 1939, while the source record's age of 81 on 7 May 2020 implies 1938 or 1939 depending on his birthday. No authoritative source reviewed gives a complete date, so birth_day, birth_month and birth_year remain unproposed.

The University of Miami states that he was born and raised in Madinah. Lower-quality biographies also associate his family with Hail, but that does not displace the explicit institutional birthplace evidence.

The University of Texas currently describes him as founder and chairman of Rashid Engineering, and no sale, exit or death was found. The firm's complete current ownership and financial scale are private, so primary industry and current Founder relationship are strong but not conclusive.

The 2025 flynas prospectus records a substantial direct stake under the full patronymic. It is treated as a secondary investment and does not displace Rashid Engineering as the documented source of wealth or justify an aviation tag.
The surviving Rashid Engineering web domain appears in business directories but could not be verified as an accessible first-party site. It is therefore not proposed as a Company Website.

Searches found multiple LinkedIn and other social profiles belonging to unrelated or insufficiently documented people named Nasser Al-Rashid. No identity-verifiable personal LinkedIn, Instagram or personal website was found, and the existing Wikipedia profile is left unchanged.

Broad Self-made is supported by his establishment and growth of Rashid Engineering. The evidence does not establish his family finances or initial launch capital, so neither self-made subtype is inferred.

Engineer is the minimum useful approved active tag. Generic philanthropy tags are excluded by policy, while construction subindustry tags would overstate a consultancy whose documented work spans multiple kinds of public project.

The existing biography is stale and source-facing: it centres an unsupported millionaire label and explains the absence of a Forbes ranking rather than the subject's durable work. It is therefore represented as correct_existing with the exact saved HTML and replaced by the validated 51-word biography.
All four vessel relationships in the source record are historical. They are used only for identity resolution where independently corroborated and are excluded from biography and wealth reasoning.
